Triggers.value: Night-time or waking up in the dark

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I drink alcohol, take medication or use drugs

vignette: Mark, a 33-year-old European American graphic designer, sought help after experiencing increasing difficulties following a traumatic encounter with law enforcement. The event occurred during an argument with his ex-wife, which escalated to a police intervention at their home. Mark was forcibly restrained and taken into custody despite his attempts to explain the situation. His traumatic experience left him feeling humiliated and helpless. Since that night, Mark has struggled with specific triggers that have become increasingly potent. He finds himself avoiding nighttime or waking up in the dark as it reminds him of being alone and vulnerable. The darkness conjures vivid images of the police car outside his home and the harsh lights from their flashlights. This fear is so profound that he often covers his face with his hands, trying to block out these intrusive memories. His job as a graphic designer has also become a source of stress due to its urban setting. He avoids crowded places, which remind him of being surrounded by people during the incident and feeling isolated in the chaos. Additionally, Mark meticulously avoids any uniform or weapon-related imagery, even going so far as to change channels if he sees police uniforms on television. Mark's efforts to cope with these triggers have led him to rely heavily on maladaptive strategies. He began drinking alcohol more frequently, particularly at night, to numb his anxiety and the vivid memories that come with darkness. The fear of reliving the traumatic event through flashbacks is overwhelming, and he has found that substance use helps mask those feelings temporarily. One evening, after a particularly stressful day at work where he had to attend a crowded meeting, Mark turned to alcohol again. As he sat alone in his apartment, the darkness outside only amplified his anxiety. He felt trapped and helpless, much like he did during the police intervention. The images of being restrained and taken into custody were seared into his mind, making it impossible for him to relax. This cycle has been relentless over the past few months. Mark had come to believe that drinking was a necessary escape from the overwhelming memories and triggers. However, this coping mechanism has led to significant disruptions in his daily life. He has missed deadlines at work due to hangovers and has become increasingly isolated, even avoiding social gatherings with friends. What frightened him most was how these maladaptive strategies were starting to take over his life. The substance use provided temporary relief but only deepened the sense of helplessness he felt about managing his triggers effectively. Mark finally sought help because he realized that his coping mechanisms were not sustainable and were leading to more problems than solutions. He is most hoping for a way to regain control over his life and reduce the intensity of these intrusive memories without relying on substances. He fears being trapped in this cycle forever, unable to escape the vivid reminders of the traumatic encounter with law enforcement.
